(Per: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE A. M. BADAR)
9 21-06-2023 Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant / First Informant in this appeal challenging acquittal of the respondent No.2 of the offence punishable under Section 4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act as well as under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. It is argued on behalf of the appellant that the learned Trial Court has committed serious error in law by disbelieving clear, cogent and trustworthy evidence of the victim female child who is categorically deposed that she was Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.171 of 2022(9) dt.21-06-2023 subjected to penetrative sexual assault by the respondent No.2

. It is further argued that medical evidence is totally unnecessary for making out the offence punishable under Section 4 of the POCSO as well as under Section 376 of the IPC, if evidence of the victim of the sexual offence is trustworthy and clear.

It is further argued that the victim female child was subjected to medical examination Hira Ali vs The State Of Bihar on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19375488/
1 after two days of the incident and, therefore, possibility of non-finding of injuries on her person was there and this factor was totally irrelevant for recording acquittal in respect of the alleged offence.

entities.text: Hira Ali vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3. We have also heard the learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No.1 /
State.
4. Perused the impugned judgment and order of acquittal of the respondent No.2 of the offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC as well as under Section 4 of the POCSO.
Instead, he is convicted of the offence punishable under Section 376 read with Section 511 of the IPC and under Section 8 of the POCSO.

5. The reasoning given by the learned Trial Court for acquitting the respondent of the offence of penetrative sexual assault is to the effect that the report of medical examination of the victim female child is not supporting the prosecution case as Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.171 of 2022(9)
dt.21-06-2023 in medical examination of the victim of the crime in question, no injuries were found on her person.

6. It is well settled that in cases relating to sexual offence on woman and more particularly minor female child, the Court is required to adopt sensitive approach and the Court is not to be swayed by minor inconsistencies or irregularity in evidence.
Prosecution case is required to be considered in broader perspective.
Similarly, non-finding of injuries on the person of the victim of the crime in question is of no consequence in such cases.

In Ranjit Hazarika vs State Of Assam reported in (1998)
8 SCC 635, the opinion of the Doctor was to the effect that no rape appears to have been committed because of absence of rupture of hymen and injuries on the private part of the victim of the crime in question.

entities.text:
Ranjit Hazarika vs State Of Assam reported in (1998)
8 SCC 635
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the Apex Court took a view in that matter that medical evidence cannot throw over board and otherwise cogent and trustworthy evidence of the prosecutrix.

Similar is the ratio of judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of B. C. Deva @ Dyava vs State Of Karnataka reported in (2007) 12 SCC 122.
7.

entities.text: B. C. Deva @ Dyava vs State Of Karnataka reported in (2007) 12 SCC 122
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this view of the matter, the following orders:-
Admit.
Issue notice of final hearing to respondent No.2. Patna High Court CR.

In the meanwhile, action under Section 390 of Cr.P.C.
to follow.
